note: What tools/personalize.mjs changes on a customer's copy of the Ember Roasters demo from the questionnaire answers (seed/questions.json: name · sector · contact). Same five kinds as Tracy Business (D38): `identity` is written exactly from the answers (a missing answer EMPTIES the field, never keeps the demo value); `replace` rewrites the demo brand everywhere; `copy` is prose a model writes for the sector, the demo text being the length reference; `facts` are claims about a real business (counts, prices, years, named clients, named people) and are REMOVED, never invented; `blocks` and `rewrite` let the model redo whole cards and entries for the sector. Values use {name} {NAME} {initials} {phone} {address} {hours} {year} {sector}. A contact line the customer did not give (phone, e-mail, address, opening hours: the questions never ask for them) keeps the template's value as a placeholder the customer fills in later (`"unanswered": "keep-demo"`); a rule with `requires` is written only when every fact it names is given.
copyNote: Read by Tracy's template readiness check, not by tools/personalize.mjs (TCH #1013, D6 + D7): demoCompanyNames is every spelling of the demo company's name, each renamed by a replace rule above; keptText is demo text kept on purpose (collection/slug for an entry, collection/slug.field for one field). Every `*image_alt` kept describes a demo picture that stays on the customer's site (this template draws no new pictures: `images` is empty), so the words still match the picture. The same holds for the `alt` of each photo in `home.space_photos` (the shop photos on the home page stay too).
labelsNote: The entries whose labels tools/personalize.mjs translates when the root is written in another language than its own (chromeLabelsOf, TCH #1013): the chrome (header, footer, search, 404) and every page's own headings, buttons, eyebrows and captions; the menus are translated beside them. Addresses, names and fields another rule decides are left alone.
